Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old woman presenting with a 2-week history of right knee pain and clicking after initiating longer distance running, concerned about injury.

History:
- Primary complaint: Right knee pain with clicking, onset approximately 2 weeks ago after increasing running distances during marathon training.
- Timeline:
  - No prior significant joint problems; minor knee injury with bruising during ice hockey a few months prior, now resolved.
  - Began marathon training about a month ago; increased running distance to 7-8 miles.
  - Knee pain starts after ~20 minutes of running (approx. 2.5-3 miles) and is sometimes severe enough to stop running.
  - Intermittent, transient swelling after first run (resolved after ice application), currently no swelling reported.
  - Episodic clicking in the knee on flexion/extension, particularly during abdominal exercises at the gym.
  - Recent single episode of tingling noted in right toes after a run; no ongoing sensory deficits.
  - Occasional mild lower leg/ankle indentation from socks after prolonged standing; no persistent swelling.
  - No locking, giving way, or instability of the knee. No problems with stairs, walking, or full range of motion.
  - No other joint pain, swelling, or back pain; no pain in hands, feet, elbows, or wrists.
- No constitutional symptoms (fever, feeling unwell), no redness, persistent heat, or restricted movement currently.

Past Medical History:
- Remote significant right knee bruise from fall during ice hockey (a few months ago), resolved.
- Hyperopia (farsightedness); status-post LASIK surgery.
- History of severe UTI; required ER visit, possible consideration for kidney stones; no chronic sequelae mentioned.
- No reported chronic GI, respiratory, or other systemic medical issues.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen, as needed, max 400 mg at a time, for joint pain.
  - Aleve (Naproxen?), dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Vitamin D, dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Melatonin, dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Xanax (Alprazolam), occasionally for insomnia, dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Regular participation in sports and exercise: gym a few times a week, marathon running.
- Occasional cannabis use: "sometimes will smoke a joint."
- Denies or not documented: tobacco smoking (cigarettes) or alcohol use.
- No mention of occupation, living situation, or financial matters.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed/documented (remote video consult, symptom inquiry only).

Investigations:
- No prior or current investigations/imaging performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:

Issue 1: Right knee pain and mechanical symptoms (clicking) after increased exercise
- Likely overuse or overtraining injury given timing after marathon training, no current signs of acute ligamentous rupture/instability, no major swelling or locking.
  - Recommend ongoing ice therapy.
  - Advise reduction in running/training volume—avoid running if painful enough to stop activity.
  - Prescribe stronger anti-inflammatory medication to be taken with food (specific agent not named in transcript).
  - Referral to physiotherapist for detailed knee assessment and management; physiotherapy recommended as initial treatment.
  - Consider further clinical examination in-person if symptoms persist or appointment with physiotherapist is delayed.
  - May require imaging (e.g., MRI) if assessment by physiotherapist indicates possible cartilage or ligament injury.

Issue 2: Transient tingling in right toes after running
- Self-limited, not currently present; monitor for recurrence.
  - Advise to report if persistent sensory changes, numbness, or weakness develop.

General plan/safety netting:
- Advise urgent review if development of persistent knee swelling, redness, heat, fever, systemic symptoms, or inability to bend/straighten knee (locking).
- Will send prescription (stronger anti-inflammatory) to patient's pharmacy and arrange physiotherapy referral.

Quality checks:

● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies status not documented.
  - Family history not documented.
  - Detailed medication reconciliation (doses/frequencies/routes) incomplete for several drugs.
  - No in-person physical exam findings.
  - Social history missing specifics on tobacco/alcohol use, occupation.
● Internal conflicts:
  - None identified.
● Transcript quality: Good overall, stream-of-consciousness patient style, but clinically relevant elements retrievable. Noisy only in patient’s ambiguous drug recall and class (Aleve/acetaminophen confusion), but no clinical impact on immediate plan.
